time_of_day: any; avoided the chaotic open as a beginner
universe_filter: liquid futures where you can quote the bid/offer
conditions: Get filled on your bid only when there is visible size/support at that price so you can exit at the same price
Immediately offer one tick above the fill
entry_trigger: passive fill at your bid when you believe you can scratch at that price
stop: exit at breakeven if the market looks like it will turn; hard cap of about 1-2 ticks (5-10 index points), never more
target_or_exit: one tick of edge (offer one tick above entry)
management: no averaging; losses above the cap are not allowed
stated_edge: Queue position and a known exit price let you collect the spread while keeping losses tiny; profit comes from rarely losing more than a tick.
stated_stats: about 28.5k USD in a month with only two small losing days (late 1990s)
data_needed: Level 2 / order book and queue position; tick data
mcf_translation: Not translatable to bar data. The transferable piece is a hard per-trade loss cap in R and a daily audit of any loss above 1R.

setup_name: Escalator up, elevator down: buy sharp sell-offs in uptrends
universe_filter: stocks with clear relative strength (rising trend visible on a zoomed-out chart)
conditions: Long-term chart clearly trending up (higher highs)
A sharp, fast sell-off occurs inside that uptrend
entry_trigger: buy into the sharp sell-off (not specified more precisely)
stop: not specified; 'play defense and get out' if it does not work
management: never short a strong uptrend because it looks overvalued
stated_edge: Strong names keep getting stronger; sharp dips in healthy uptrends are buying opportunities while counter-trend shorts get run over.
mcf_translation: Daily: close > 50d and 200d SMA and 3-month return in top quintile; trigger when the stock falls > 2 ATR over 1-3 days (or RSI(2) < 10); buy next open; exit on close below 50d SMA or after N days. Compare with a pure relative-strength hold.

universe_filter: liquid large/mid-cap US stocks; exclude ETFs, ADRs, micro-caps
conditions: Compute fraction of shares outstanding sold short (or borrowed) for each stock daily
entry_trigger: long the lowest short-interest names, short the highest (or simply avoid the highest)
management: equal or rank weights; test predictive power at 1/5/10-day forward horizons
stated_edge: Short sellers pay to borrow and tend to be informed money, so heavy short interest flags trouble ahead.
mcf_translation: Not directly; could be used as a filter on MCF long setups (skip longs with high short interest) if a short-interest feed were added.

setup_name: Gun-maker stocks after mass-shooting or gun-control news
conditions: A mass-shooting event or political gun-control announcement occurs (hand-labelled event dates)
Optionally hedge with shorts in the same sector or the broad market
entry_trigger: buy the gun-maker basket after the event date
target_or_exit: hold for a fixed window after the event (not specified), flat otherwise
management: cap each name's weight; hedge sector/market exposure to isolate the relative effect
stated_edge: Consumers tend to buy more guns after such events, especially when restrictions are threatened.
stated_stats: reported 'fairly good returns' in the historical window studied (no numbers)
mcf_translation: Daily bars only: with a hand-made event-date CSV, buy the basket (e.g. SWBI, RGR, AOUT/VSTO) at next open, hold N days, compare with XLY/SPY-hedged return.

setup_name: Correlated key-level confluence (3 of 4 indices hit levels together)
instrument: futures (NQ traded; ES, RTY, YM as confirmation); also gold vs silver/copper/platinum, crude vs RB/HO
time_of_day: regular session; about 5-6 trades/day; flat by close
universe_filter: a family of 4 instruments that react to their levels together
conditions: Each instrument has daily key levels computed before the open (fixed, single price, not zones)
At least 3 of the 4 instruments touch a level of the same type (all support or all resistance) within about the same 1-minute bar (seconds apart)
The 4th instrument does not contradict (not touching an opposing level)
Each instrument has enough room to its next opposing level for at least 3:1 reward-to-risk
entry_trigger: limit order at the traded instrument's level at the moment of synchronous touch: buy at support, sell at resistance
stop: fixed-size tight catastrophe stop, with a small buffer allowed if a correlated market still needs to retest its own level
target_or_exit: partial exit when a correlated instrument reaches its opposing level; runner held toward the instrument's own next level
management: move stop to breakeven plus commission after a set fraction of the expected move; trail the rest; flat by end of day
stated_edge: Large players' activity shows up as simultaneous reactions at the same levels across correlated markets; agreement filters out false level touches.
stated_stats: about 85% win rate reported by followers of her live room; 5-6 trades/day; losing day about 1 in 5
data_needed: her proprietary level model; futures data; options data feeding the levels
mcf_translation: Proxy with SPY/QQQ/IWM/DIA 1-5 min bars and standard pre-open levels (prior-day high/low/close, overnight high/low, pivot S1/R1). Signal when 3 of 4 ETFs touch a level of the same type within the same 1-min bar and the 4th is not at an opposing level; enter QQQ at its level; stop 0.25-0.5 ATR(5m); partial at the first opposing level hit by any ETF. Compare with single-ETF level touches to measure the value of the confluence filter.

setup_name: Front-run the fund roll in commodity futures
time_of_day: days around the scheduled roll window
universe_filter: commodity futures with large passive/index fund positions rolling on a known schedule
conditions: Identify which side the funds roll (e.g. sell front month, buy next month)
Position in the spread ahead of the roll window
entry_trigger: enter the calendar spread before the roll period begins
target_or_exit: exit into the roll flow (sell to or buy from the rolling funds)
stated_edge: Large predictable roll flows push the spread; being positioned ahead lets you supply liquidity to them.
data_needed: futures curve data and roll calendars
mcf_translation: Not testable on MCF stock bars; a loose stock analogue is index-rebalance or month-end flow studies on daily bars.

setup_name: Buy right-tail convexity in crypto options when vol is cheap
conditions: Market has sold off and implied volatility is low relative to history
Call overwriting supply has damped upside implied vol
Vol term structure inverted so longer-dated options are relatively cheap
entry_trigger: buy out-of-the-money calls (long gamma), favouring cheaper later expiries
target_or_exit: not specified; profit from convex gains on a sharp upside move
stated_edge: Market makers underprice the fat right tail of crypto returns and covered-call selling cheapens upside vol.
data_needed: crypto options chains and implied-vol history
mcf_translation: Not translatable to MCF stock bars.
